page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, the instance allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint stands at 16.0 GB, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The architecture incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. Network capability features a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution for standard compute tasks. Stress-ng yielded scores of 1,850.49 in single-core and 7,748.54 in multi-core metrics, aligning with Geekbench results of 1,452.0 single-core and 5,294.0 multi-core. Software compilation under Clang scored 8,140.0, while PassMark registered a CPU mark of 11,125.79. In web tier and data processing benchmarks, the instance sustained 7.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.62 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, memory subsystem testing highlighted significant bottlenecks: large-block uncached read bandwidth measured 21.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 23.88 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem within the lower tier of cloud benchmarks. Furthermore, medium LLM inference for 7B parameter models proved sluggish, achieving only 15.4 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 5.54 tokens/sec for text generation.

The hardware configuration yields solid cost efficiency for CPU-focused application stacks that do not require massive memory footprints or fast local scratch disks. The 1:2 memory ratio ensures operational expenditure remains concentrated on raw CPU cycles rather than unused memory headroom. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is well positioned for software build runners, containerized backend services, API routing layers, distributed batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines.
